consequences: CC-D10 can close endpoint, cross-partition reference, context, and stateful admission semantics against one accepted graph rather than choosing governance topology.

A future governance implementation must replay accepted ProtocolLedger events into the protected partition and enforce pre-event authority, external-root, direct non-self-amendment, and epoch boundaries without adding a governance-specific graph identity or query surface.
constraints: ProtocolLedger remains the sole write authority and authoritative event history; it is neither an accepted-graph partition nor the same physical store as the graph.
Replay derives domain or governance membership only from the GovernedGraphContract or GovernanceContract admission path, never caller data, record type, name, namespace, or storage convention.
Governance mutation uses pre-event authority state seeded by exactly one external genesis root; missing or ambiguous roots refuse and graph writes cannot create, replace, or delete the root.
Same-event authority cannot authorize its event. When the authority source is a governance policy, its identity must differ from the directly mutated governance-policy identity.
Ordinary-path events cannot directly mutate governance identities. Cross-partition references, endpoints, reads, context, and exact stateful admission remain with OD-010.
A policy-instance update under the same GovernanceContract preserves the composition epoch; a semantic GovernanceContract change requires the new D06 composition and epoch.

The historical GovernancePolicyGraph remains Open. Same-type GovernancePolicyGraphR2 supersedes it with status Excluded; OD-007 rejects R2 exactly; the selected protected topology has no supersedes edge to either alternative; no effective-current query rule is introduced.

Existing typed policy artifacts remain protocol-ledger artifacts. Exact records, operations, wire and API fields, policy language, bootstrap encoding and replacement, authentication, read policy, storage, migration, recovery, monitoring, and implementation remain deferred.
data.selected_option: One protected replay-derived governance partition inside the accepted graph

summary: Accept one protected replay-derived governance partition in the accepted graph.
why: The protected partition keeps one accepted graph lineage and query surface while separating ordinary mutation from governance mutation. Pre-event authority, one external root, direct policy non-self-amendment, and D06 epoch identity provide the minimum integrity boundary without a second graph, synchronized heads, policy language, storage design, or implementation.
